question: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?

raiseTranscript.text: On my first project, the dashboard showed 15% drop in conversion after a UI change, but the PM and designer kept saying users loved the new flow from their interviews. I pulled the raw event logs myself and found the tracking tag was firing twice on the new button.
I walked through the exact user sessions with the data, showed the duplicate events, and fixed the tag. Conversion recovered once we had clean numbers.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?
Role: new grad on first feature team
Situation: post-launch conversion drop vs PM/designer interview feedback
Actions: pulled raw logs, found duplicate tracking tag, walked through sessions
Outcome: fixed instrumentation, numbers recovered
Quote: "I walked through the exact user sessions with the data"
Follow-up: Asked what they did next; they described fixing the tag and verifying
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Dive Deep for junior level. Candidate owned their own instrumentation bug instead of stopping at conflicting signals. They went to raw logs rather than accepting either the dashboard or the anecdotes. Quote about walking through exact sessions shows they did the detailed work themselves. Biggest strength is taking personal responsibility for reconciling the mismatch at the data level instead of escalating or ignoring it.

lowerTranscript.text: The metrics said one thing but the team thought it was fine so I just reported both and moved on.
Did you look at the raw data?
Not really, I figured the PM knew what was going on.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?
Role: new grad
Situation: vague metrics vs team opinion
Actions: reported both sides, did not investigate
Outcome: moved on
Quote: "I figured the PM knew what was going on"
Follow-up: Asked about raw data; candidate had not looked
junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar on Dive Deep. Candidate accepted the conflict without digging into root cause and deferred to the PM. No evidence of examining raw data or attempting to resolve the discrepancy themselves. The story stays at the level of reporting rather than investigating, which is below expectations even for junior individual contributors.

raiseTranscript.text: Two teams had conflicting views on whether a new recommendation model improved retention. Product said yes from qualitative feedback, but the A/B test showed flat results. I pulled per-cohort retention curves and found the lift was real only for users acquired in the last 30 days.
How did you influence the teams?
I ran a follow-up analysis segmented by acquisition channel and shared the cohort tables with both teams so they could see where the model actually moved the needle.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?
Role: senior on recommendation platform
Situation: product qualitative vs A/B test flat on retention
Actions: built cohort curves, segmented by acquisition channel, shared tables
Outcome: teams aligned on targeted rollout
Quote: "I ran a follow-up analysis segmented by acquisition channel"
Follow-up: Asked how they influenced; they described sharing segmented tables
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Dive Deep for senior. Candidate did not stop at the surface A/B result and instead built deeper cohort views that explained the disagreement. The follow-up segmentation created clarity that both teams could act on. Biggest strength is using detailed analysis to resolve cross-team conflict without authority, which is the expected senior behavior.

lowerTranscript.text: The test was flat but product was pushing for launch so I flagged the mismatch in the weekly sync and let leadership decide.
Did you do any deeper cuts?
I didn't have time to segment further before the decision meeting.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?
Role: senior
Situation: flat A/B vs product push
Actions: flagged in sync, no further analysis
Outcome: deferred to leadership
Quote: "I didn't have time to segment further"
Follow-up: Asked about deeper cuts; candidate cited time constraints
senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar on Dive Deep for senior. Candidate identified the conflict but stopped at flagging it instead of driving resolution through additional analysis. Lack of segmentation or follow-up investigation means the disagreement remained unresolved by data. This is below the cross-team influence expected at senior level.

raiseTranscript.text: Business reviews showed strong top-line growth but regional leaders insisted churn was rising in key markets. I commissioned a full customer-level cohort rebuild across all regions and discovered the growth was coming from low-LTV segments while high-value cohorts were churning faster than reported.
I paused the new market expansion, reallocated marketing spend to retention programs for the high-value segment, and reset the board forecast with the corrected cohort view.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?
Role: exec overseeing growth
Situation: top-line growth vs regional churn signals
Actions: commissioned full cohort rebuild, identified LTV skew, paused expansion
Outcome: reallocated spend and reset forecast
Quote: "I paused the new market expansion"
Follow-up: Asked about trade-offs; they described pausing expansion and resetting forecast
exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Dive Deep for exec. Candidate drove an org-wide data rebuild that revealed a strategic mismatch between reported growth and actual cohort economics. The decision to pause expansion based on the deeper view shows long-term judgment over short-term optics. Biggest strength is using detailed analysis to change business direction at scale rather than defending the existing narrative.

lowerTranscript.text: The numbers looked good overall so I told the regions their local data must be incomplete and kept the expansion plan.
Did you validate the cohort view yourself?
I trusted the central dashboard and moved forward.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time the data and what people were telling you disagreed. What did you do?
Role: exec
Situation: growth vs regional churn reports
Actions: dismissed regional input, trusted central dashboard
Outcome: kept original plan
Quote: "I trusted the central dashboard and moved forward"
Follow-up: Asked about validation; candidate did not investigate
exec.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar on Dive Deep for exec. Candidate overrode field signals without deeper investigation and protected the existing plan. No evidence of personally driving cohort-level analysis or adjusting strategy based on the mismatch. This reflects poor strategic judgment at the org level.
